Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12414 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective immediately, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a). The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

Section 2 requires the parties to submit final offers within 30 days after creation of the board and the board to report its selection of the most reasonable offer within 30 days after the final offers. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

Section 4 provides that the board terminates upon submission of the report under section 2. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12414 (48 FR 14861, Federal Register of April 6, 1983; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between The Long Island Rail Road and Certain Labor Organizations and signed April 4, 1983. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain labor organizations. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 4 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (sec1; sec2; sec3; sec4). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12414 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; they are not recorded as later events because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
